title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand what polyglot is: a NetOps + ISP management backend exposing MCP, REST, and WebSocket/SSE for multi-vendor network automation. Then check go.mod to see the stack — Gin, GORM, ConnectRPC, whatsmeow, scrapligo, go-routeros.

title: Application Entry Point
description: cmd/server/main.go boots the server: it loads configuration, connects Postgres/Redis, wires the driver registry, and starts the Gin HTTP router, ConnectRPC services, and WebSocket streaming.

title: Composition Root & Configuration
description: internal/app/app.go is the dependency-injection hub wiring every adapter and use case together. internal/config/config.go loads runtime settings from the environment (documented in .env.example).

title: Port Contracts
description: The port layer defines the interfaces everything else depends on — DeviceDriver (execute/classify/translate), repositories, credential vault, LLM provider, audit writer, and streaming drivers. Adapters and drivers implement these.

title: Domain Model
description: internal/domain holds pure business entities and rules — device, command, session, customer, subscription, plan, billing. command.Command and its policy define what can be executed and what needs approval.

title: Use Cases
description: internal/usecase orchestrates single operations by calling ports — ExecuteCommand validates and runs a command through the driver, StreamOutput pipes live device output. Use cases never touch vendors directly.

title: Device Drivers
description: internal/driver contains one folder per vendor. Mikrotik speaks the RouterOS API via go-routeros; genericssh/generictelnet share a scrapligo engine driven by YAML platform definitions. Commands are classified destructive vs read-only per vendor.

title: Driver Registry
description: internal/registry selects and caches the right driver per device based on vendor and driver type, handing out ready-to-use connections.

title: Adapters — API Surface
description: Handlers in adapter/connect expose ConnectRPC services, adapter/mcp exposes MCP tools for LLM agents (get_device_status, run_command, push_config), and adapter/ws streams device output over WebSocket. The proto files in api/proto define the wire contracts.

title: Adapters — Persistence, Auth, AI
description: Postgres repositories implement the storage ports with GORM; Casbin + JWT enforce RBAC; LLM adapters (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Groq) back the assistant; Redis caches; the vault keeps device credentials encrypted.

title: Data Layer
description: Migrations create the schema — devices, bots, customers, and more. The devices table shows the columns the device model maps onto.

title: Deployment & CI
description: deployments/docker/Dockerfile builds the server image; docker-compose orchestrates server, Postgres, Redis, and WhatsApp services; the GitHub Actions workflow runs lint and tests.

title: Architecture Docs
description: Finish with Polyglot-Architecture.md and the ADRs in docs/adr to understand the why behind the design — why Gin, why driver interfaces without sessions, dual streaming connections, and scrapligo as the generic CLI engine.
